what_changed: The retirement entry now declares an *intent* per leftover stack and proves the matching fact instead of applying one stop rule to every shape. shared_writer keeps the original proof (a live co-writer on a cluster data volume, stopped by PostgreSQL Immediate Shutdown so no shutdown checkpoint lands in the WAL the survivor is using, redis by SIGKILL so no persistence write lands in the shared volume). serving_publisher is the opposite proof: the container owns no cluster data directory, so it is stopped with the signal its own image declares, and the plan must prove it shares no *live writable* volume with anything still running.

A serving declaration must name what could still revive it (revival_path), may not contain a postgres/redis container (that is the shared_writer shape), and every serving container must declare the exact signal docker stop will send (expected_stop_signal). An image that later changes its declared signal refuses instead of being stopped with an unreviewed signal.

The collector reads Config.StopSignal with Docker's documented default SIGTERM resolved explicitly (Docker 27 omits the key entirely when unset, which is why an empty string would have been read as 'no signal'), plus per-container mounts and a running-only volume-owner map. Sharing is judged against live co-owners only: sc_dev_odoo_data is still attached to the stopped prod odoo container, and reading the stopped attachment as a second writer would have refused a clean publisher retirement.
